content: Indication-Specific Dosing for Lily of the Valley (Convallaria majalis): Oral Administration (PO): Average daily dose: 600 mg/day. Tincture: Up to 6 g/day, divided into three doses (TID). Liquid extract: 600 mg/day, divided into three doses (TID). Dried extract: 150 mg/day. Therapeutic Uses: Used for circulatory disorders, heart palpitations, arrhythmias, congestive heart failure (CHF), cardiac edema, cardiac asthma, kidney stones, bladder stones, and urinary tract infections (UTIs). Contains cardiac glycosides similar to those found in digitalis. Drug Interactions: 1. Digoxin and Lily of the Valley: Both substances increase each other's toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Diuretics (e.g., bendroflumethiazide, bumetanide, chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, cyclopenthiazide, ethacrynic acid, furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, methyclothiazide, metolazone, torsemide): These drugs increase the toxicity of Lily of the Valley due to potassium (K+) depletion, which raises the risk of cardiac toxicity. Use with caution and monitor closely. 3. Laxatives (e.g., senna): Increases the risk of cardiac toxicity due to potassium depletion. Use with caution and monitor closely. 4. Calcium Salts (e.g., calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate): These compounds enhance the effects of Lily of the Valley through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Antiarrhythmic Agents (e.g., amiodarone, disopyramide, encainide, flecainide, ibutilide, lidocaine, mexiletine, procainamide, propafenone, quinidine, sotalol): These drugs may increase the toxicity of Lily of the Valley due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Beta-Blockers (e.g., acebutolol, esmolol, propranolol): These drugs may increase the toxicity of Lily of the Valley due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Calcium Channel Blockers (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil): These drugs may increase the toxicity of Lily of the Valley due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Adenosine: May increase the toxicity of Lily of the Valley due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Phenytoin: May increase the toxicity of Lily of the Valley due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Contraindications and Precautions: High Blood Pressure, Kidney or Liver Disease, and Potassium Deficiency: Use with caution due to the increased risk of adverse effects. Pregnancy: Use only under qualified supervision, as overdosing can be potentially fatal. Overdosing may cause nausea, vomiting, headache, stupor, color vision disturbances, and irregular heartbeat. Pregnancy Category: Avoid use. Lactation: No available data (N/A). Toxicity and Overdose Risks: Taking more than the recommended dose can result in severe side effects, including nausea, vomiting, headache, stupor, disturbances in color perception, and irregular heart rhythms. The presence of cardiac glycosides in Lily of the Valley makes it particularly dangerous in cases of overdose. This information highlights the importance of careful monitoring and professional supervision when using Lily of the Valley, especially in patients with pre-existing conditions or those taking interacting medications.
